publishedExpectations.claim: BlackRock's careers home: 'Clients turn to us – as both an asset manager and leading provider of financial technology – for the innovative solutions they need when planning for their most important goals.'
BlackRock for Universities grew from a 2019 hackathon idea and integrates Aladdin so students can analyze portfolios more effectively, bridging academic learning and professional investment practice.
The careers site states 'BlackRock's tech careers offer diverse and dynamic opportunities with personalized career paths and continuous learning' and highlights internal mobility stories.
The careers portal organises hiring around Life at BlackRock, Student & Graduate programmes across Americas/EMEA/APAC, and experienced-professional openings.

notes: BlackRock's careers site confirms the asset-manager-plus-fintech positioning and names Aladdin, which drives the skill profile: portfolio analytics, risk, and Python data engineering rather than low-latency trading. Community-reported patterns (unverified): online coding assessments (HackerRank-style) and HireVue video screens for graduate technology roles, followed by behavioural interviews; no retrieved official page documents these formats. Quant-dev candidates should weight portfolio theory, statistics and data-platform skills over market microstructure. The site itself publishes no technical bar beyond degree-level qualifications, so treat any specific test names as unconfirmed.
